skill.name: openserv-multi-agent-workflows
skill.description: Guides developers through OpenServ multi-agent workflow design with runnable examples, API patterns, trigger setup, task dependencies, and troubleshooting guidance.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot OpenServ multi-agent workflows with practical examples.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The high-impact confirmed findings are credential-handling patterns in runnable examples, especially WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY usage. Most external command, system reconnaissance, and hardcoded URL findings are false positives caused by Markdown, TypeScript template literals, and documented OpenServ endpoints. Additional context concerns involve paid x402/on-chain wallet workflows and local tunnel exposure. Static review was capped at 400/444 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 44 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Examples repeatedly handle wallet private keys and API keys through .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings to use development wallets, avoid production funds, exclude .env from source control, and rotate exposed keys immediately.

remediation.issue: The paid image workflow combines x402 payments, payout routing, and ERC-8004 on-chain registration.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to review price, wallet address, gas costs, and chain actions before running paid or on-chain examples.

remediation.issue: The local agent run path can expose the local process through a built-in tunnel.
remediation.suggestion: Document tunnel behavior, expected callers, shutdown steps, and safe test inputs before users run the local agent.

content.value_statement: Complex OpenServ workflows require correct agent discovery, task edges, triggers, and authentication. This skill provides practical examples and troubleshooting steps for designing multi-agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains workflow creation with workflows.create, workflow.sync, and provision patterns.
Shows complete examples for blog, content, video, podcast, crypto, and paid image pipelines.
Documents agent discovery through marketplace search and owned agent lookup guidance.
Covers webhook triggers, x402 paid triggers, task dependencies, and workflow edges.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for missing edges, trigger activation, and wallet setup.
Highlights clean graph design patterns for sequential, fan-out, and conditional workflows.
limitations: The skill is documentation and examples, not a hosted workflow runner.
Examples require OpenServ platform access and valid credentials before they can run.
Some examples involve wallet keys, paid triggers, or gas costs that need careful review.
OpenServ APIs can change, so users should verify the installed skill version.

use_cases.title: Create a Research Pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan a workflow where one agent researches a topic and another produces publishable content.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a simple OpenServ workflow with one webhook trigger, one research task, one writing task, and the required edges.

prompt_templates.scenario: Modify an existing example for a new content workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OpenServ workflow examples to adapt the content creation pipeline for my topic, agents, trigger inputs, task names, and output format.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Workflow Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Troubleshoot workflows where tasks do not run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my OpenServ workflow plan and identify missing edges, inactive triggers, dependency issues, or agent assignment problems.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for x402 and on-chain registration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the paid image pipeline guidance to design a paid OpenServ workflow, including wallet handling, x402 trigger setup, agent tasks, and safety checks.

output_examples.input: I need a workflow that turns a topic into a blog post.
output_examples.output: A sequential plan with a webhook trigger, research task, writing task, required edges, activation steps, and test request guidance.

output_examples.input: My trigger fires, but no tasks start.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist that checks workflow edges, trigger activation, running state, agent assignments, and dependency configuration.

output_examples.input: I want to monetize an image generation workflow.
output_examples.output: A paid workflow design covering x402 trigger price, payout wallet handling, custom agent provisioning, image agent selection, and review warnings.

best_practices: Start with a linear workflow, then add fan-out or branching only when the data flow is clear.
Define explicit edges between triggers and tasks so the workflow graph can execute reliably.
Use dedicated development credentials and wallets when testing examples that handle secrets or payments.
anti_patterns: Do not connect every task to every other task without a clear data dependency.
Do not assume task dependencies replace workflow edges in OpenServ workflow setup.
Do not run paid or wallet-based examples without reviewing credential storage and cost impact.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design OpenServ workflows where multiple agents collaborate through triggers, tasks, dependencies, and edges.

faq.question: Does this skill run workflows by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples that you adapt and run with OpenServ platform tools.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why are workflow edges important?
faq.answer: Edges connect triggers and tasks in the workflow graph. Tasks may not execute correctly without them.

faq.question: Does it cover paid workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an x402 paid image pipeline and ERC-8004 registration guidance.

faq.question: What should I review before running examples?
faq.answer: Review wallet private key handling, API keys, paid triggers, platform permissions, and external agent choices.
